page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs, mapped from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, and is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing users to attach external storage volumes.

Benchmark results position the D16s_v4 consistently in the average tier across multiple performance vectors. The CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1412.09 and a multi-core score of 14877.24, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 15816.41. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 830.85 GB/sec, which drops to 73.63 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write bandwidth of 44.64 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 12.09 GB/sec and processed 13.9 million Redis SET operations per second.

The lack of local storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, making this instance unsuitable for heavy local disk caching or hardware-accelerated graphics rendering. For language model workloads, the instance handles small 135M models adequately, but performance drops to the bottom 25% tier for prompt processing on medium 7B models, and large 70B models are unsupported. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a stable resource density for standard enterprise workloads. The D16s_v4 is suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
